 Judgment

1. Being aggrieved of the Award passed by the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch granting compensation of an amount of Rs. 16,80,000/- along with interest @ 9% per annum in favour of the petitioners/respondents No. 1 to 4 herein, widow, daughter and parents of the deceased- Khursheed Ahmed, who died in a road accident on 13.08.2018, the appellant-Insurance Company has filed the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
2. In order to understand the controversy in its right perspective, it would be appropriate to give the brief facts of the case.

3. On 13.08.2018, the deceased-Khursheed Ahmed was travelling in the offending vehicle bearing registration No. JK02AC-0074 which was driven by the respondent No. 3 rashly and negligently when it met with an accident near Gursai Pamranar, as a result whereof the deceased- Khursheed Ahmed succumbed to his injuries.
The deceased at the time of accident was doing masonry and carpentry work and was earning Rs. 30,000/- per month.
4. The deceased had left behind his widow, daughter and parents who filed the petition before the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch.

5. The Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch vide order dated 29.11.2021 granted compensation of an amount of Rs. 16,80,000/- while assessing the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.
12,000/- but after deducting 1/4th towards his personal living expenses, the same was assessed as Rs. 9,000/- per month.

6. The appellant-Insurance Company has challenged the impugned award on the following grounds:
(a) That the Presiding Officer, MACT, Poonch while passing the impugned Award has not appreciated the law as well as facts on record in a proper perspective.
(b) That the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the permit conditions and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, the appellant- Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Shaneez Akhter on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38568609/
2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: (c) That as per the permit conditions and the conditions of the insurance policy, the maximum carrying capacity of the offending vehicle is 7+1 but actually the offending vehicle was carrying passengers far above the permissible limit and thus the permit conditions and the conditions of the insurance policy had been violated by the owner of the vehicle, therefore, the insurer-Oriental Insurance Company Limited is not liable to indemnify the insured.

(d) That respondents No. 1 to 4/claimants have not been able to prove that the deceased was working as skilled labourer and making a monthly earning of Rs. 12,000/- per month, as no cogent and reliable documentary evidence had been placed on record.

The bald assertion of PW-1 Shaneez Akhter, totally uncorroborated by any documentary evidence with respect to material facts and material particulars, loses any significance and becomes totally irrelevant as far as either the determination of the compensation amount or returning a finding even with respect to basic entitlement to claim compensation is concerned.

However, in the face of the evidence adduced by the respondents No. 1 to 4/claimants and also taking into account that the respondents No. 1 to 4/claimants could not produce any supporting evidence, the learned Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch should have taken Rs. 8,000/- as the monthly income of the deceased.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

Learned counsel for the appellant has, inter alia, argued that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving lience at the time of accident, as such appellant-insurance company is not liable to indemnify the deceased; that the Presiding Officer,
Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch has not rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 12,000/- and thirdly that the President Officer has not applied his mind while granting compensation in favour of the claimants.

9. So far as the first argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident is concerned, the Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch has observed in his Award that the appellant has failed to prove any evidence in proof of the said fact.

The Presiding Officer has also observed that in case there is no such endorsement to ply the commercial vehicle found in the licence, simply for that reason the claim of the victim of an accident or otherwise to say 3rd party claim cannot be over thrown which is statutory right to claim the compensation of said 3rd party or victim of the accident in case injury is suffered by him or in the event of death to claim compensation by the dependency of the deceased for loss suffered, as such the appellant-insurance company is also legally and statutorily bound to pay the compensation.
10.

So far as second argument that the Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Poonch has not applied its mind while assessing the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 12,000/- is concerned, the Presiding Officer, after carefully examining the witnesses including the respondent No. 1, whereby they have deposed that the deceased was a skilled labourer and was earning Rs.

3 36,000/- per month, has assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 12,000/- after taking into consideration the factor that the deceased was a skilled labourer.

sentences.text:
11. So far as third argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that the President Officer has not applied his mind while granting compensation in favour of the claimants is concerned, it is established from the perusal of the record that the Presiding Officer has dealt with the claim petition inasmuch as the defence set up by the appellant herein before it rightly and consequently passed the impugned award which, in the facts and circumstances of the case, cannot be found fault with, more so, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in case titled as "Anita Sharma and ors vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd and Anr" reported in 2021 (1) JKJ (SC) 140 wherein at para 22, it has been observed as under:
"22.

entities.text: Anita Sharma and ors vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd and Anr" reported in 2021 (1) JKJ (SC) 140
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Equally, we are concerned over the failure of the High Court to be cognizant of the fact that strict principles of evidence and standards of proof like in a criminal trial are inapplicable in MACT claim cases.
The standard of proof in such like matters is one of the preponderance of probabilities, rather than beyond reasonable doubt.

One needs to be mindful that the approach and role of Courts while examining evidence in accident claim cases ought not to be find fault with non-examination of some best eye witnesses as may happen in a criminal trial; but, instead should be only to analyse the material placed on record by the parties to ascertain whether the claimant's version is more likely than not true."
12.
For what has been observed, considered and analysed above, the impugned award does not call for any interference.
Resultantly, appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed.
